message.content:
**October 26, 2026 (announced and rolled out that day).**[[1]](https://9to5mac.com/2026/10/26/openai-upgrades-chatgpt-and-codex-with-new-gpt-6-1-terra-model/)

**Canonical URLs:**
- Official blog post: https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-1-terra/ (referenced directly in OpenAI's X posts and consistent with the naming pattern of prior GPT-6.1 releases such as Sol).[[2]](https://x.com/dgrreen/status/2114795869195338125)
- Related official system card addendum: https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-6-1-terra (published the same day, explicitly referencing "the blog" for the model description).[[3]](https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-6-1-terra)
- Official X announcement from @OpenAI (posted ~18:06 UTC on Oct 26, 2026), with a follow-up from @OpenAIDevs.[[4]](https://x.com/OpenAIDevs/status/2114780986613682473)

**Availability sentence (quoted from OpenAI's X post accompanying the announcement):** "GPT-6.1 Terra is rolling out now and is available to all Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex. Developers can also access it through the OpenAI API as gpt-6.1-terra."[[2]](https://x.com/dgrreen/status/2114795869195338125)

This aligns with contemporaneous reporting (e.g., 9to5Mac on the same day: "The new GPT-6.1 Terra model is available today through ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API") and the system card's statement that the model was being introduced that day as a fast, efficient upgrade focused on professional work, visual reasoning, and computer use (with pricing roughly 50% lower than GPT-5.6 Terra).[[1]](https://9to5mac.com/2026/10/26/openai-upgrades-chatgpt-and-codex-with-new-gpt-6-1-terra-model/)

No earlier official blog or X post for GPT-6.1 Terra was found; prior GPT-6.1 Sol announcements followed a similar pattern in September 2026. The page and posts confirm the canonical sources above.
